answer: Cross-epoch spectral fingerprinting: each agent hashes its transaction graph into a fixed 256-bit sketch per epoch, tinted by an umber decay vector weighting recent edges. Identity persistence requires Jaccard similarity above τ between consecutive sketches. Sybils spinning fresh keys show near-zero overlap and diverge; a wharf of coordinated clones must sustain shared subgraphs across many epochs. Attacker cost: maintaining plausible plume of correlated history for N identities scales O(N·epochs) in storage and graph-forging work, while honest sparse agents pass cheaply.
